minutes.headline: Lunenburg senior tax relief was signed into law Jan 6; COA also approved a letter urging Mark Connect to add Worcester hospital rides.
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging heard from former select board member Lou Franco that the governor signed Lunenburg's senior tax relief law, then a long presentation inviting seniors to a Feb 3 session on exemptions, deferrals and the circuit breaker. The Eagle House Supporters introduced their new board, and the council read an update on the Nashoba Valley Medical Center. Members approved two sets of minutes, a letter on Mark Connect rides, and a liaison to the supporters group.

A FY26 capital plan item for architectural design of the parking lot exists; may stay regardless of building plans.
The last installment was October and another is expected in April; paperwork is filed.
Funding already allocated for the kitchen; target completion end of June.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging heard that the governor signed Lunenburg's senior tax relief law, and was told how it works and how seniors apply.
A presentation invited seniors to a Feb 3 session on tax exemptions, deferrals and the circuit breaker.
A motion to send a letter asking Mark Connect to add Worcester-area hospital trips was made; the outcome was not audible.
A motion to appoint a liaison to the Eagle House supporters group was made; the outcome was not audible.
Members approved minutes, agreed to invite Michael Ray back on school-owned land and the parking lot, and heard the FY26 budget needs little discussion.

why_it_matters: Senior homeowners may be able to lower a tax bill through the new relief law, exemptions, deferrals or the circuit breaker, and the Feb 3 session is where the council planned to explain how to apply.
Whether the council asked Mark Connect for Worcester hospital rides, and whether a liaison was appointed, cannot be confirmed from the recording, so the official minutes are the place to check.
